correctness.rationale: For any \(1/2<p<1\), \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) and \(N=2m\ge4\), each start-positive word is enumerated by odd/even switch run compositions; start-negative paths reflect the occupancy index. Three exact binomial identities give the two central adjacent differences and hence formula (1) without normalization ambiguity. The Laurent coefficient representation C_j=[z^j](1+uz)^n(1+uz^-1)^n ensures \(C_1>C_2\ge0\) by strict symmetric-convolution unimodality; it yields \(\theta_m<2u/(1+u)\) for every finite n. The difference of two iid Binomial(n,u/(1+u)) variables has span one, positive variance and an aperiodic lattice local CLT, so \(C_2/C_1\) tends to one and theta_m tends to 2u/(1+u). Together these show the iff uniform boundary and the eventual reverse sign below it. The \(N=4\) threshold \(u\) and exact \(N=10\) example yield the reversal. Standalone checker was run from its actual source path and passed 680 exact-rational Markov-recursion comparisons; these are a finite cross-check, not the proof of universal quantifiers. Endpoints \(p=1/2\) or \(p=1\) are excluded, no claim of global modal optimality.

originality.rationale: The result is the exact initial-bias threshold for a strict comparison of two adjacent central occupancy bins simultaneously at every even length, including an explicit short-to-long sign reversal. Pemmasani (2026, full arXiv v1) assumes a fair start and studies central-versus-endpoint crossings, not the nonstationary-start adjacent-center comparison. Dekking and Kong (2011, inspected original arXiv full text, Proposition 4.1/4.3, Theorem 4.1) give a general starting-law probability mass function, interior log-concavity and a qualitative global shape classification; none states the all-even-length boundary \(\alpha+p=3/2\) or parameter-region reversal. Their results do not logically imply the threshold without a new coefficient comparison and a sharp asymptotic analysis. The inaccessible Renshaw-Henderson 1981 full text is an unresolved priority risk. Searches against published mathematical records and existing claims did not identify a covering theorem; this is not proof of exhaustive novelty.

value.rationale: Initial direction bias affects the central shape of correlated-walk occupation laws in a way that changes with trajectory length. Determining the exact half-plane \(\alpha+p\ge3/2\), valid at every even finite length, and a strict nonempty region of short-to-long reversal is a natural structural modal question, not a routine increment or a lone numerical check. It cleanly separates transient initial-state skew from asymptotic central lattice corrections and complements the fair-initial-state endpoint-crossing problem. The result is a complete two-parameter all-even-length phase boundary for this exact local observable, with sharp necessity and an explicit finite witness. It does not need to imply a higher-dimensional general theorem to be mathematically useful.
